# UX Requirements Quality Checklist: Folder scope for Browse and search

**Purpose**: Validate the *quality* of this feature's UI requirements — completeness, clarity, consistency, measurability, coverage. These items test what the spec **says**, not what the code **does**.
**Created**: 2026-08-04
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md), [contracts/scope.md](../contracts/scope.md)

**Note**: Generated by `/speckit-checklist`. Run *after* the feature shipped, deliberately, as a test of whether the command finds anything the implementation review missed. Read the Findings section at the end before acting on individual items.

**Status, 2026-08-04: 10 of 24 closed, 14 open.** A closed item carries ✅ and what closed it. **An open item is a documentation gap, not a defect** — every one asks whether something is *written*, and in each case the implementation already behaves sensibly. That distinction is the point: the code was right and the requirements were thin, so nothing was fixed and five properties were specified.

Open: `CHK001` `CHK003` `CHK004` `CHK005` `CHK006` `CHK007` `CHK008` `CHK009` `CHK011` `CHK014` `CHK020` `CHK021` `CHK022` `CHK023`.

These are **not tracked by `0018`'s follow-up ledger**, which covers decision-record commitments only. Widening it to checklist items would need a record, and would be the wrong trade: 14 documentation gaps on a shipped v1.1 feature are a reading list, not debt with a due date. If one becomes work, it becomes a record or a feature and *then* the ledger sees it.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 - Are requirements defined for a panel containing more folders than fit the available height? [Gap] — the implementation chose a 168 px scroll cap; neither `spec.md` nor `contracts/scope.md` §3 states any bound
- [x] CHK002 - Is the behaviour specified when only **one** source is registered? [Gap] — the implementation hides the panel entirely below two sources, a behaviour no requirement describes  ✅ **closed:** FR-019 — specified 2026-08-04; behaviour was correct, never described
- [ ] CHK003 - Are requirements defined for how a source name too long for the panel is presented? [Gap] — truncation, wrapping and tooltip fallback are all unspecified
- [ ] CHK004 - Are interaction-state requirements (hover, focus, active, disabled) defined for the folder rows? [Gap] — `contracts/scope.md` §3 specifies location, content, counts and bulk action, but no states
- [ ] CHK005 - Are requirements defined for the panel's behaviour at small **viewport heights**? [Gap] — §9's responsive rules address narrow widths; a short window must divide space between the panel and the artifact list, and no requirement says how
- [ ] CHK006 - Is the **ordering** of folder rows specified? [Gap, Ambiguity] — config order, alphabetical and by-artifact-count are all defensible and the spec picks none
- [ ] CHK007 - Are requirements defined for what the per-row **count** represents — every artifact in that source, or only those matching the current query? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-001] — FR-001 says "artifact count" without fixing which

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK008 - Is "above the existing type groups" precise enough to place the panel unambiguously? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001] — it does not say whether the panel sits inside or outside the search wrapper, which changes what scrolls
- [ ] CHK009 - Is the visual signal for "a scope is in force" specified, beyond the count text itself? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009] — the implementation colours the count with the accent token; FR-009 requires only that the count be *stated*
- [x] CHK010 - Can "§9's existing tokens and the established chip/pill vocabulary" be checked objectively? [Measurability, contracts §3] — no requirement enumerates which tokens are permissible, so conformance is currently a judgement  ✅ **closed:** §9 token check in npm test — literals and undefined tokens both caught
- [ ] CHK011 - Is the `outside scope` chip's tone specified relative to the verdict chip beside it? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007] — FR-007 fixes the wording and forbids "badge", but not whether the chip reads as neutral or as a warning

## Non-Functional Requirements — Accessibility

- [x] CHK015 - Are keyboard-operability requirements defined for the folder checkboxes? [Gap, Coverage] — `contracts/scope.md` §3 Keyboard covers `↑/↓` over the list and `⌘K`, and says no new keybinding is added, but never states the panel must be reachable or operable by keyboard  ✅ **closed:** FR-015 — rows are <button>; asserted by test
- [x] CHK016 - Are requirements defined for how tick state is exposed to assistive technology? [Gap] — the implementation sets `aria-pressed`; no requirement asks for it, so it is an accident rather than a commitment  ✅ **closed:** FR-016 — aria-pressed; asserted by test
- [x] CHK017 - Are focus-visibility requirements specified for the folder rows? [Gap] — §9 assigns the accent token to focus, but no requirement applies it here  ✅ **closed:** FR-017 — §9 global focus floor; panel opt-out asserted against
- [x] CHK018 - Is a non-colour signal required for "in force", for readers who cannot distinguish the accent token? [Gap, Coverage] — the count text changes colour only  ✅ **closed:** FR-018 — ☑/☐ glyph and `all` vs `3/16`; both asserted

## Findings — read this before working the items

Generated after the feature shipped, as a test of the command. Being honest about the result matters more than the item count.

**Genuinely found, and not caught by implementation review or `/speckit-analyze`:**

- **CHK001, CHK002, CHK005** — three real, undocumented implementation decisions. The 168 px scroll cap, hiding the panel below two sources, and behaviour at short viewport heights are all choices made while coding that no requirement describes. CHK002 is the sharpest: the panel *disappears* under a condition nothing in the spec mentions.
- **CHK015–CHK018** — the accessibility gap is systematic, not incidental. The feature's requirements never mention keyboard operability, focus visibility, assistive-technology state, or a non-colour signal. The implementation happens to be keyboard-operable because the rows are `<button>` elements, and happens to set `aria-pressed` — both accidents rather than commitments, which is exactly the distinction a requirements checklist is for.
- **CHK006, CHK007** — two live ambiguities. Row ordering and what the count means were decided in code without the spec ever choosing.
- **CHK020** — the structural point beneath most of the above: **no success criterion covers appearance at all.** SC-001…SC-007 are about filtering, persistence, reachability and the index invariant. That is why CHK010's "§9's tokens" cannot be answered objectively today.

**Already closed, listed so they are not re-opened:** the `Folders all` wording (CHK013) and the single bulk action (CHK012) were both amended on 2026-08-03 after `/speckit-analyze` found them. CHK019's SC-007 was restated on 2026-08-04. CHK024's edge-case list is complete.

**Limits of this artifact.** Every item asks whether something is *written*, never whether it *looks right*. The panel could be specified to four decimal places and still be ugly, and nothing here would notice. It found a real accessibility hole and three undocumented decisions; it cannot tell you the sidebar is cramped.
